description: Change an image's pixel dimensions, keeping its proportions, on-device (same high-quality resampler and encoders as ruah.tools). Give exactly one of max_side (the longest side in pixels — e.g. 1920 for web pages, 1080 for social posts, 640 for thumbnails) or percent. It never enlarges unless allow_upscale is true. Saves a new file and reports the size before and after; the original is never changed. The output is also compressed with the same format/quality options as `compress`, so "make it 800px and WebP" is one call.

allow_upscale.description: Allow max_side to make the image larger than the original. Default false.

format.description: Output format: keep = same as the input; webp = usually smallest, keeps transparency; avif = smaller still, slower; jpeg = photos only, transparency becomes white; png = keeps transparency. Default keep.

input_path.description: Image file to resize. Absolute, ~/…, or relative to the working directory.

lossless.description: png only: keep exact colours (bigger files).

max_side.description: Fit inside this many pixels on the longest side.

output_path.description: Where to save. Default: "<name>-resized.<ext>" next to the input. Existing files are never overwritten.

percent.description: Scale to this percentage of the original (1–100; to enlarge, use max_side with allow_upscale).

quality.description: 1–100 for webp/avif/jpeg. Default 80 (visually near-identical, much smaller).

name: resize
title: Resize image
